market.geography_note: No drive-time catchment was established. Public evidence covers Morton demographics and approximate straight-line competitor bands only. [E029, E030, E037]

market_demand_supply_rationale.verified_fact: Morton has 16,595 residents, median household income of 94,402, 25.9% under age 18, and 23.1% age 65 or older. [E029, E030]
market_demand_supply_rationale.inference: The income and age mix support a cautious demand-fit hypothesis, but supply balance, growth, payer mix, and a true catchment were not measured.

competitive_pressure_rationale.verified_fact: The public scan found a nearby direct peer, regional specialty overlap, retail substitution, and a medical/surgical system; approximate distances are straight-line rather than drive time. [E021, E022, E023, E024, E025, E026, E027, E037]
competitive_pressure_rationale.inference: Pressure is likely meaningful but cannot be quantified with confidence without a deduplicated provider set, drive times, patient-choice counts, and comparable reputation data.

room_to_win_rationale.verified_fact: This score is the required inverse of the Competitive Pressure Index: 100 minus 56.
room_to_win_rationale.inference: The number describes room relative to the public pressure read, not measured market share or demand.

practice_competitiveness_rationale.verified_fact: Vintage has specific specialty pages, three listed optometrists, an on-site lab, a linked booking flow, sound crawl hygiene, and first placement in seven sampled searches. [E002, E003, E004, E005, E006, E008, E012, E013, E014, E015, E016, E017, E018, E019, E020]
practice_competitiveness_rationale.inference: Those signals justify a competitive public-position band, not a market-leader claim; the search sample is not a rank grid and peer review volume was unavailable.

client_opportunity_rationale.verified_fact: Vintage already presents multiple specialty capabilities, credible professional authority, online booking, and directional search visibility. [E002, E003, E004, E005, E009, E010, E012, E013, E014, E015, E016, E017, E018, E020]
client_opportunity_rationale.inference: The most actionable upside is to test conversion, access, and trust loops before adding services or broad awareness spend.

specialty_options.inference: Measure the existing lanes together before choosing which one merits more capacity or promotion.
specialty_options.why: Capability is visible; conversion, capacity, continuation, and economics are unknown.
disconfirmers: Existing specialty conversion and capacity may already meet owner-set thresholds.
Regional competitors may own referral relationships that public pages do not reveal. [E023, E024, E025]

specialty_options.verified_fact: Vintage names IPL, radiofrequency, and low-level light therapy; regional competitors also show dry-eye programs. [E002, E023, E024]
specialty_options.inference: A credible existing lane with demand-fit proxies, but not proven white space.
specialty_options.why: The 65-plus share supports a demand hypothesis, while competitor overlap argues for conversion testing rather than an ownership claim. [E030]
disconfirmers: Local treatment demand may be lower than the age proxy suggests.
Competitors may have stronger capacity, outcomes, pricing, or referrals.

specialty_options.verified_fact: Vintage offers four named myopia approaches; 25.9% of Morton residents are under 18; Vision Care Center offers overlapping approaches. [E003, E025, E030]
specialty_options.inference: The family-age proxy makes a small conversion/referral test reasonable, but it does not establish demand.
specialty_options.why: Visible capability plus a relevant age segment, tempered by documented competition and no inquiry or start data.
disconfirmers: The under-18 population may not translate into qualified myopia demand.
Capacity or payment acceptance may constrain the lane.

specialty_options.verified_fact: Vintage names scleral, RGP, and Ortho-K options, and Paul Velting has independent AOA contact-lens authority signals. [E004, E009, E010]

disconfirmers: Public authority may not translate into practice-level demand.
The workflow may depend on one clinician or have limited capacity.

white_space.verified_fact: Four specialty pathways are publicly visible. [E002, E003, E004, E005]
white_space.inference: The first white space is operational: learn which existing pathway converts and retains before adding another.
white_space.why: This is a measurement wedge, not a claim of unmet patient demand.

white_space.verified_fact: Vintage has online first-available booking, while Focus On Eyes publishes weekday and Saturday hours. [E020, E022]
white_space.inference: A short access diagnostic can determine whether any calls or appointment intent cluster outside current availability.
white_space.why: No leakage is assumed; the test resolves the uncertainty cheaply.

white_space.verified_fact: Vintage has AOA authority and directional search visibility, while at least one result still shows the prior address. [E009, E010, E012, E013, E014, E015, E016, E017, E018, E031, E032]
white_space.inference: A controlled recall/referral/review/listing baseline can test whether existing trust is being compounded consistently.
white_space.why: This favors verification and maintenance over broad awareness spend.

recommended_actions.small_test: Choose one of dry eye, myopia, specialty contacts, or Neurolens. For four weeks, count aggregate qualified inquiries, consults booked, consults completed, and starts by source. Use no patient-identifying fields.
recommended_actions.proof: A complete four-step weekly funnel exists and reveals the largest drop-off, or shows no meaningful drop-off.
recommended_actions.stop_condition: Do not add a service or spend more on promotion if conversion and capacity already meet thresholds set by Vintage.
recommended_actions.verified_fact: Vintage already presents four specialty pathways. [E002, E003, E004, E005]

recommended_actions.small_test: Aggregate appointment-intent contacts by weekday and hour, then record answered, booked, and first-available outcome. Compare with the current booking path and published competitor-hour context.
recommended_actions.proof: The practice can identify whether a recurring access gap exists by hour or service.
recommended_actions.stop_condition: Keep current hours and staffing if no meaningful loss cluster appears.
recommended_actions.verified_fact: Vintage exposes online first-available booking and Focus On Eyes publishes Saturday access. [E020, E022]
recommended_actions.inference: The contrast justifies a diagnostic, not a claim that Vintage is losing demand.

recommended_actions.action: Audit one trust loop and current address consistency
recommended_actions.small_test: For four weeks, track one aggregate loop, either recall, referral, review request, or optical follow-through. Separately verify whether the live prior-address result is editable.
recommended_actions.proof: One loop has a baseline from eligible event to completed outcome, and each editable high-visibility listing shows the current address.
recommended_actions.stop_condition: Do not launch a new campaign if the chosen loop and live listing set already meet thresholds set by Vintage.
recommended_actions.verified_fact: Vintage has independent authority and sampled search visibility; a public result still surfaces the former address while the practice site shows the current address. [E009, E010, E012, E013, E014, E015, E016, E017, E018, E031, E032]
recommended_actions.inference: Existing trust may be more valuable to systematize than broad awareness is to buy.

data_quality.limitation: Scores use conservative rubric bands because the public set does not support complete peer percentiles or source-of-record catchment math.
strong_sources: Official Vintage service, team, location, sitemap, and booking pages [E002, E003, E004, E005, E006, E007, E008, E019, E020, E032]
American Optometric Association authority evidence [E009, E010]
Official competitor service pages [E021, E022, E023, E024, E025, E026, E027]
weak_sources: One-date search and Maps samples [E011, E012, E013, E014, E015, E016, E017, E018]
Straight-line geocoding rather than drive time [E037]
One lower-quality directory result for prior-address residue [E031]
missing_to_upgrade: Drive-time catchments and a deduplicated office/provider inventory
Comparable review count, recency, themes, and response behavior for Vintage and Tier 1 peers
A formal local rank grid plus authorized GBP/GSC and website conversion data
Authorized aggregate call, booking, no-show, recall, referral, optical, and specialty-funnel summaries
Service-line capacity, continuation, payer, collections, and profitability data

disconfirmers: The seven-query sample may not reproduce across devices, locations, dates, or a formal local rank grid. [E012, E013, E014, E015, E016, E017, E018]
Focus On Eyes may capture more routine demand than public pages reveal because of local tenure and published access. [E021, E022]
Vision Care Center may have a stronger specialty position than this scan captures because it publicly names advanced dry-eye diagnostics and overlapping myopia options. [E024, E025]
Vintage's visible specialty breadth may not translate into available capacity, completed starts, continuation, or practice-level economics. [E002, E003, E004, E005]
Straight-line distances may materially misstate practical patient choice and travel willingness. [E037]
Professional authority may be concentrated in one doctor rather than transferred through the practice team and workflows. [E006, E009, E010]
